page: Microsoft Azure DC96ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor featuring 48 dedicated physical cores and 96 virtual CPUs via two threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2.

Memory capacity is configured at 384.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage includes a bundled 3,865 GB solid-state drive (SSD), providing substantial local disk space for high-throughput scratch space or caching without requiring auxiliary block storage attachments. The instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not feature hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight robust parallel processing and throughput. While single-core performance measured 2,331.96 on stress-ng, falling within the average baseline, the multi-core stress-ng score reached 110,733.6, placing the instance in the top 25 percent tier. In in-memory data store tests, the server completed 91.97 million Redis SET operations per second, also placing in the upper quartile of benchmarked instances.

The combination of 96 dedicated threads, balanced system memory, and 3,865 GB of fast local SSD makes the DC96ads_v5 cost-effective for resource-dense horizontal workloads. The architecture is well matched for distributed enterprise databases, large-scale Redis or Memcached clusters, data transformation pipelines, and parallel continuous integration builds that benefit from high multi-threaded compute density and local disk access.
description: Microsoft Azure DC96ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture using Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 96 vCPUs across 48 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system features 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a standard 4.0 GB per-core allocation, along with 3,865 GB of integrated local SSD storage. The platform omits dedicated GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Performance evaluations indicate average single-core capability with a stress-ng score of 2,331.96, countered by strong multi-core scalability reaching 110,733.6 and Redis SET throughput exceeding 91.97 million operations per second, both ranking in the top quartile. These hardware specifications make the instance effective for distributed in-memory caching systems, database hosting, batch ETL processing, and large multithreaded enterprise applications requiring significant local disk capacity.
